items.prompt:
You left your satchel somewhere in the ruins. Write a tiny text adventure to go and get it back: rooms are a dict of dicts, commands come from `input()`, and what you pick up goes into a list.

The rooms are given in `ROOMS`. Each room has a `description`, its `exits` (a dict from direction to room name) and its `items` (a list). Four stages: read a command, move, pick things up, then the whole game.

Hard mode starts from an empty page, so here is the map to copy:

```python
ROOMS = {
    "gate": {"description": "A broken gate. A path leads north.", "exits": {"north": "hall"}, "items": []},
    "hall": {"description": "A hall of fallen pillars. Exits: south, east.", "exits": {"south": "gate", "east": "vault"}, "items": ["lamp"]},
    "vault": {"description": "A quiet vault. Your satchel lies here!", "exits": {"west": "hall"}, "items": ["satchel"]},
}
```

Stage 1: `parse(command)` returns a `(verb, noun)` pair in lower case, ignoring extra spaces: `parse("Take Lamp")` is `("take", "lamp")`, `parse("take old lamp")` is `("take", "old lamp")`, `parse("look")` is `("look", "")` and `parse("")` is `("", "")`.

Stage 2: `move(rooms, here, direction)` returns the room that exit leads to, or `here` when there is no exit that way.

Stage 3: `take(rooms, here, item, satchel)` moves `item` from the room's items into the `satchel` list and returns `True`. If the item is not in the room it changes nothing and returns `False`.

Stage 4: `play()` starts in `"gate"`, prints its description, then reads commands with `input()` until `quit` (print `Bye!`). `look` prints the description, then `You see: ...` if there are items. `go DIR` prints the new room's description, or `You can't go that way.`. `take ITEM` prints `Taken: ITEM` or `There is no ITEM here.`; taking the satchel prints `Taken: satchel`, then `You found the lost satchel. Well done!`, and ends the game. `inventory` prints `Satchel: lamp, map` or `Satchel: (empty)`. Anything else prints `I don't understand.`
